amendments.operational_classification: post-provider resource ownership, watchdog establishment and verified teardown
amendments.what: post-provider resource ownership in SessionRunner.create(): the pod id, start epoch, actual costPerHr, provider_resource_created and one_use_grant_consumed are assigned, persisted and saved, and the detached watchdog is started, BEFORE the returned price is judged. An over-price resource is then classified as a post-provider consumed abort and torn down through the canonical teardown_now() with provider confirmation, instead of a one-shot unconfirmed 'remove pod' issued before the resource was ever registered.
amendments.why_the_owner_is_shared_session_runner: the defect is in SessionRunner.create(), the only place a returned provider id is parsed, and registration must happen at that parse. Every downstream owner -- the watchdog, teardown_now, run_session's exception handler -- keys on self.pod_id, so no caller can repair it from outside. Phase A, Phase B, the continuations and the preflight share this code and share the defect.
amendments.why_a_c1_only_override_was_rejected: a C1-only create() override would leave every other session with an unowned billing pod on the same path, and would create a second deletion implementation beside teardown_now -- the exact duplication the review forbade.
